name: Eave
summary: Collects continuous meteorological data using an ESP32 connected to a precision BME280 sensor (temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric barometric pressure) and an external rain droplet sensor, calculating barometric altitude and storm forecasts displayed on a 0.96" OLED.

parts.name: ESP32 NodeMCU DevKit V1
parts.why: Performs atmospheric pressure trend regression and drives I2C OLED display

parts.name: BME280 Atmospheric Pressure, Temperature & Humidity
parts.why: Measures atmospheric pressure (±1 hPa), temperature (±0.5°C), and humidity (±3%)

parts.name: FC-37 Rain & Water Droplet Sensor
parts.why: Detects the onset of rain droplets and measures precipitation intensity

parts.name: 0.96 inch I2C OLED Display (SSD1306)
parts.why: Displays barometric trend icons, current weather forecast, temperature, and humidity

parts.name: Single 18650 Li-ion Battery Holder
parts.why: Powers off-grid weather monitoring with deep-sleep power management

parts.name: 170 Tie-Point Mini Solderless Breadboard
parts.why: Convenient compact breakout module for power distribution

buildSteps: Step 1: 3D print the louvred Stevenson-screen Eave enclosure base and canopy lid in white PETG.
Step 2: Snap the ESP32 board into the inner mounting rails with antenna oriented towards the vent side.
Step 3: Mount the Bosch BME280 sensor module inside the sheltered louver chamber.
Step 4: Attach the FC-37 rain sensor grid to the exterior roof canopy at a 30-degree incline for drainage.
Step 5: Connect I2C lines from both the BME280 and SSD1306 OLED in parallel to pins D21 (SDA) and D22 (SCL).
Step 6: Route the rain sensor analog signal to pin D34 through the weather grommet.
Step 7: Power on via USB or 18650 battery cell, calibrate sea-level barometric offset, and place outdoors.

agentLog.detail: Parsed request: Micro-weather station with barometric pressure, rain detection, and display.
Selected ESP32, BME280, FC-37 Rain Sensor, and SSD1306 OLED. Total BOM: ₹1,090.
Designed multi-device I2C bus on D21/D22 with pull-ups and analog rain sense on D34.
Generated sketch.ino with pressure trend storm forecasting and rain threshold logic.
Compiled target esp32:esp32:esp32 successfully (flash: 238 KB, RAM: 17.5 KB, 0 errors).
Simulated rain drop transition: verified serial prints RAIN_ALERT when D34 falls below 2500.
Generated OpenSCAD Stevenson screen with 30-degree louvers preventing precipitation ingress.
Environmental airflow clearance check passed: 18 mm cross-flow channel across BME280.
